newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Digital Equipment firms. [CORRECTED 22:17 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Digital Equipment firms. [CORRECTED 22:17 GMT]

text.p: Shares in Digital Equipment Corp rose in pre-open U.S. trade on Thursday, boosted by better-than-expected second quarter earnings.
Digital shares were up 2-1/2 to 36-5/8 (corrects price) after the personal computer maker reported earnings per share of $0.15 against $0.91 a year ago.
The First Call consensus estimate had been for a profit of $0.10 a share as the company moved away from a first quarter loss.
The Maynard, Mass., company is expected to give more details at a conference call scheduled for 1030 EST/1530 GMT.

General Electric Co shares were not active. The company reported fourth quarter earnings per share of $1.26 against $1.12 for the same period a year ago. However, traders said the share was being bid up 1/2 to 103-1/8 because of the earnings.
"Apparently that looks like the number it's going to start at," one trader said.
Apple Computer Inc was down 3/8 to 16-7/8 after reporting a loss of $120 million, or $0.96 a share, in its first quarter against a loss of $69 million, or $0.56 a share, in the same period last year.

Shares in Columbia/HCA Corp and Value Health Inc were largely quiet in pre-open trade as investors waited for a conference call with executives to get more details about the health care companies' $1.3 billion merger.
Value Health was trading up 1-3/4 to 22.
One trader said a flood of early-morning earnings had left traders struggling to make decisions on buys and sells.
"There's so many earnings, and things really aren't moving yet," he said.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street said Circuit City Stores Inc's rise on Wednesday had more to do with used cars than computers. The company's shares rose two to close at 33-1/8.
The company plans to begin a road show next week for the planned sale of a 20 percent stake in CarMax, its used car retailing business. The deal is roughly worth $300 million.
